record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: Within quantum gravity, can proposed solutions to the axion quality problem actually be implemented successfully, or alternatively is the quality problem itself not a genuine obstacle for the QCD axion once quantum-gravitational effects are treated correctly?

evidence.quote: A number of approaches to the axion quality problem have been proposed [136, 141–148], but it is an open question within quantum gravity to determine whether or not these approaches can be successfully implemented [149, 150] or if the quality problem itself is even of concern.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The QCD axion is a hypothetical pseudo-scalar particle arising as the pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson of a spontaneously broken global U(1) symmetry (the Peccei–Quinn symmetry) introduced to dynamically solve the strong CP problem of quantum chromodynamics. The "axion quality problem" is the observation that, since quantum gravity is generally expected to violate all continuous global symmetries, even tiny Planck-suppressed operators that explicitly break the Peccei–Quinn symmetry can shift the effective axion potential's minimum away from the CP-conserving value by an amount that exceeds the experimental upper bound on the neutron electric dipole moment, thereby spoiling the Peccei–Quinn mechanism.

Question: Within a consistent framework of quantum gravity, can any of the proposed mechanisms protecting the Peccei–Quinn symmetry from Planck-scale breaking (for example, models based on gauge symmetries, discrete symmetries, compositeness, extra dimensions, warped geometries, or non-minimal gravitational couplings) be successfully realized in a way that guarantees the required suppression of all symmetry-breaking operators? Alternatively, is the axion quality problem itself absent once quantum-gravitational effects (such as gravitational instantons, wormholes, and black-hole-mediated processes) are treated correctly, in the sense that these effects yield contributions to the axion potential that are intrinsically too small to disturb the strong CP solution?
artifact.category_tag: Axion quality problem in quantum gravity
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains actively debated. Multiple 2024–2025 works propose mechanisms (extra dimensions, warped geometry, baryon-number PQ, non-minimal couplings to gravity) to alleviate the quality problem, while a 2025 analysis of gravitational instantons argues their effects may be too small to matter. No consensus has emerged either confirming a successful implementation within a complete quantum-gravity framework or definitively dismissing the quality problem.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational instantons and the quality problem of the QCD axion
status_evidence.snippet: Reanalyzes gravity-induced PQ breaking and argues gravitational instanton contributions are too small to give a significant quality problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work argues quantum-gravitational instanton effects may not generate a significant axion quality problem.

status_evidence.title: Axion Quality Problem: Keep Calm and Baryon
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes axion as pNGB of baryon number to evade the quality problem when coupled to gravity.
status_evidence.claim: New model-building proposals continue to appear, indicating the problem is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Extra-Dimensional Axion Expectations
status_evidence.snippet: Extra-dimensional axions provide a robust realization of a high-quality axion with PQ as higher-dimensional gauge invariance.
status_evidence.claim: Various quantum-gravity-motivated frameworks are being pursued to address the quality problem.
